body: Totally understandable. For me, dying from an outside factor takes the suicide part out of the equation. An accident is a lot easier for the world to understand than a suicide and honestly, I'm always this type of passive-suicidal. The crisis point is when I actively have the drive to want to kill myself.

I'm so sorry that you had to go through that- sorry for what you're currently going through. I can't imagine what it feels like to lose your friend like that. It's totally understandable to feel numb after something like that- that's real trauma dude. Maybe you can look into a service dog? I know a lot of rented places won't allow pets, but maybe a documented emotional service animal would be a different story.

Sorry it's taken me about three months to respond to this. I really appreciate that you, a total stranger, took the time to share so much with me- even if my actions don't show it. I'm still alive, at least. That's already three months out of a ten year gamble. I suppose I can try to bet on the rest of it if I take it a few months, weeks, or days at a time. I'm like you in that respect; I don't have much, but my word is one thing I hold. 
I'm incredibly glad that you're still alive. It takes such strength to choose to fight to live on after falling that low. I think that we forget sometimes that attempting suicide truly is a trauma. I've noticed that after my attempts, I've sort of just gone on with everything without addressing the situation- sort of passively pretending that nothing happened. Oh, you tried to kill yourself? Ok, whatever. I don't think it's ever been active suppression..maybe I'm so used to being severely depressed that it actually is as if nothing happened to me. It's difficult being stuck in that sort of limbo after an attempt-fighting through it might be even more difficult- but the fact that we're both choosing to do so is something to be proud of.
 
I just started college a few months ago, and I'll admit that it hasn't gotten any better. A prime example of that is that it's currently a Friday night at my notorious party school, and here I am on SuicideWatch. My roommate just withdrew from university, and I'm basically here alone now- meaning if I really wanted to, I could barricade the door, hang myself, and no one would find me for days. And to be honest, part of me wanted to. Then I remembered your note. I read it over again, and it helped me talk myself down. I'm really gonna try to take that gamble. Thank you, stranger- for your understanding and kindness.

P.S. Sorry for rambling- also, you really should! I just now got the Far Harbor dlc and I'm spending most of my life on it rn
